simple: Protects websites, APIs and generative-AI applications from attacks (WAAP). Instead of signatures and manual rules, it uses two AI engines: one trained on millions of malicious and normal requests, the other learning the normal behavior of your specific application — so it also blocks zero-day attacks (for example, Log4Shell) with a minimum of false alarms. Stops OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQL injection, XSS, remote code execution and more), protects against more than 2,800 known web vulnerabilities (IPS), tells bots from humans and stops password guessing, credential stuffing and scraping. Finds all APIs, including forgotten ones, and checks requests against the OpenAPI schema; inspects uploaded files; for AI applications, blocks prompt injections and data leaks. In the WAF-as-a-Service option, it filters network- and application-layer DDoS attacks through global points of presence, with a 24/7 response team. Deploys as a service, in the cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), in Kubernetes or on your own servers; licensed by request volume, and an open-source version (open-appsec) is also available.
